title: John Fetterman and the Fight for White Working-Class Voters

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: We are driving north on Highway 81, approaching Scranton and about to pass an interchange for President Biden Expressway.
sentences.zh: 我们正开车在81号公路上向北行驶，快到斯克兰顿了，马上就要经过“拜登总统高速公路”的立交桥。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: You can literally see the freeway sign has been pasted over to make it the President Biden Expressway named after obviously the hometown kid.
sentences.zh: 你可以清楚地看到高速公路的路牌被覆盖了，改成了“拜登总统高速公路”，显然是以这位家乡之子命名的。

sentences.en: But yeah, there's not that many roads.
sentences.zh: 不过确实，这样的路并不多。

sentences.en: For Democrats to hold on to any power at all in Washington, they have to do what Joe Biden did in his home state of Pennsylvania two years ago.
sentences.zh: 民主党想要在华盛顿保住任何权力，就必须做到乔·拜登两年前在他家乡宾夕法尼亚州所做的事情。

sentences.en: Break the Republican Party's grip on the white working class voters who used to be at the core of the Democratic Party base.
sentences.zh: 打破共和党对白人蓝领选民的掌控，而这些选民曾经是民主党选民基础的核心。

sentences.en: The outcome is going to shape our country for decades to come.
sentences.zh: 这次选举的结果将影响我们国家未来几十年。

sentences.en: And the power to shape that outcome is in your hands.
sentences.zh: 而塑造这一结果的力量掌握在你们手中。

sentences.en: No race better encapsulates that challenge than the Pennsylvania Senate candidacy of John Fetterman.
sentences.zh: 没有哪场竞选比约翰·费特曼在宾夕法尼亚州的参议员竞选更能体现这一挑战了。

sentences.en: I know Pennsylvania well.
sentences.zh: 我很了解宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: And John Fetterman is Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 而约翰·费特曼就是宾夕法尼亚州的化身。

sentences.en: He is Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他就是宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: Today, national political correspondent Shane Goldmacher traveled to Pennsylvania to understand how Fetterman fits into the Democratic Party plan to lure those voters back.
sentences.zh: 今天，全国政治记者谢恩·戈德马赫前往宾夕法尼亚州，探究费特曼如何契合民主党吸引这些选民的计划。

sentences.en: If the plan is actually working or whether Biden was a fluke and that crucial group of voters is now a lost cause.
sentences.zh: 看看这个计划是否真的奏效，还是说拜登只是个特例，而那群关键选民现在已经无可挽回了。

sentences.en: It's Monday, November 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月7日，星期一。

sentences.en: So Shane, right before the last election, back in 2020, you went to northeastern Pennsylvania for the Daily to try to understand a pretty essential question about that race,
sentences.zh: 谢恩，在上一次选举前，也就是2020年，你曾为《每日新闻》去过宾夕法尼亚州东北部，试图弄清关于那场竞选的一个核心问题，

sentences.en: which was whether it was possible for Joe Biden to win back the white working class voters who had really abandoned the Democratic Party in large numbers four years earlier to vote for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 那就是乔·拜登是否有可能赢回那些在四年前大量背弃民主党、转而投票给唐纳德·特朗普的白人蓝领选民。

sentences.en: And that ended up being a really prescient line of reporting because that's more or less exactly what Joe Biden did, right?
sentences.zh: 事实证明，那是一次非常有预见性的报道，因为这基本上就是乔·拜登所做的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: He did it, and he did it specifically in northeastern Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他做到了，而且特别是在宾夕法尼亚州东北部做到了。

sentences.en: We have to understand that white voters without college degrees not that long ago were a competitive group between Democrats and Republicans.
sentences.zh: 我们必须明白，没多久以前，没有大学学历的白人选民在民主党和共和党之间还是一个摇摆群体。

sentences.en: And then Trump came along, and all across the country, the Republican margins grew in this group, and it grew over a couple of different issues.
sentences.zh: 后来特朗普出现了，在全国范围内，共和党在这个群体中的优势不断扩大，这是由几个不同的议题推动的。

sentences.en: There was this sense that Democrats had sort of sold them out economically, that the trade deals that they backed before had hurt them.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，认为民主党在经济上出卖了他们，他们之前支持的贸易协定伤害了他们。

sentences.en: But I think the more resonant issues have been social issues, this vision that the Democratic Party has put forth of a multi-ethnic, multicultural America that,
sentences.zh: 但我认为更具共鸣的是社会议题，即民主党所提出的那种多元种族、多元文化的美国愿景，

sentences.en: for many on the right, feels just like woke and exclusive of them.
sentences.zh: 对于许多右翼人士来说，这感觉就像是“觉醒文化”，而且排斥了他们。

sentences.en: And Trump came, and he took what had been a trend, and he magnified it.
sentences.zh: 特朗普来了，他抓住了一个趋势，并将其放大。

sentences.en: And so in 2016, Trump won in Pennsylvania partly because he just blew out Hillary Clinton among these voters.
sentences.zh: 所以2016年，特朗普在宾夕法尼亚州获胜，部分原因就是他在这些选民中以压倒性优势击败了希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: And the lesson from 2016 in Pennsylvania and all across the country is that the math for Democrats is just really hard to make work if you're getting annihilated by white voters who are working class.
sentences.zh: 2016年宾夕法尼亚州以及全国各地的教训是，如果民主党在白人蓝领选民中惨败，那么他们的选票数学就很难算得通。

sentences.en: And the reason is there's so many of them, 42 percent of the electorate in the country nationwide in 2020, were white voters without college degrees.
sentences.zh: 原因在于他们的人数非常多，2020年全国范围内，没有大学学历的白人选民占选民总数的42%。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a huge number.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个巨大的数字。

sentences.en: That's essentially an insurmountable political obstacle.
sentences.zh: 这本质上是一个无法逾越的政治障碍。

sentences.en: There's no victory in American politics, from what you're saying, without 42 percent of the vote, or some of it.
sentences.zh: 照你这么说，如果拿不到这42%选票中的一部分，在美国政治中就不可能获胜？

sentences.en: Yeah, you can't be losing by huge margins, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，你不能以巨大的差距输掉，对吧？

sentences.en: If you lose 42 percent of the electorate by a 70-30 margin, the math just becomes nearly impossible to close the gap everywhere else.
sentences.zh: 如果你以70比30的比例输掉42%的选民，那么在其他任何地方弥补差距几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: And it's one of the reasons that Pennsylvania is a real target for the Republican Party, and frankly, across the old industrial MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 这也是宾夕法尼亚州成为共和党重点目标的原因之一，坦率地说，整个老工业区的中西部地区都是如此。

sentences.en: These are places with an outsized portion of white voters without college degrees, the very people that Trump activated and turned into more solid Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这些地方有很大比例的白人蓝领选民，正是这些人被特朗普激活，变成了更坚定的共和党支持者。

sentences.en: And so when Biden was running in 2020, his promise was, look, I'm going to slow this down, if not reverse it.
sentences.zh: 所以当拜登在2020年参选时，他的承诺是：看，我要放缓这种趋势，如果不能扭转的话。

sentences.en: And that's what he did.
sentences.zh: 而他确实做到了。

sentences.en: He ran as a moderate, as a person who could win the backing of police unions and firefighting unions.
sentences.zh: 他以温和派的身份参选，作为一个能赢得警察工会和消防员工会支持的人。

sentences.en: He tried to take positions that didn't turn off these voters culturally or economically.
sentences.zh: 他试图采取一些在文化或经济上不会让这些选民反感的立场。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so when the results came in in 2020, and you looked at the map, you could see that Joe Biden had improved all across the state in those exact communities.
sentences.zh: 所以当2020年的结果出来，你查看地图时，可以看到乔·拜登在这些特定社区的得票率在全州范围内都有所提升。

sentences.en: Trump was still winning, but Democrats weren't losing as badly as they did with Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 特朗普依然获胜，但民主党并没有像希拉里·克林顿时期输得那么惨。

sentences.en: So it's not quite right to think of him as winning anything back so much as just losing it by less.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其说他赢回了什么，不如说他只是输得少了点。

sentences.en: Yeah, it wasn't the only reason he won Pennsylvania or the presidency, but it was a key part of the demographic shifts that put a Democrat back in the White House.
sentences.zh: 是的，这并不是他赢得宾夕法尼亚州或总统大选的唯一原因，但这是将民主党人送回白宫的人口结构变化的关键部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in doing what Biden did with white working class voters in northeastern Pennsylvania, he created a model for Democrats,
sentences.zh: 通过拜登在宾夕法尼亚州东北部对白人蓝领选民所做的一切，他为民主党创造了一个模式，

sentences.en: not to reverse what Trump achieved with that demographic, but to meaningfully blunt it.
sentences.zh: 不是为了扭转特朗普在这一人群中取得的成就，而是为了有效地削弱它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this time around, I wanted to come back to northeastern Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 所以这一次，我想回到宾夕法尼亚州东北部，

sentences.en: because the challenge that Democrats have with the white working class voters here is the challenge they have all over the country.
sentences.zh: 因为民主党在这里面对白人蓝领选民的挑战，就是他们在全国各地面临的挑战。

sentences.en: And it's the challenge that's going to determine whether they can control the Senate and keep hold of Congress.
sentences.zh: 这也是决定他们能否控制参议院并保住国会控制权的挑战。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And there's one race in particular, the Senate race in Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 有一个特别的竞选，即宾夕法尼亚州的参议员竞选，

sentences.en: that's seen as perhaps the likeliest single seat to determine whether Democrats or Republicans are in control of the Senate next year.
sentences.zh: 被视为最有可能决定明年民主党或共和党谁能控制参议院的单一席位。

sentences.en: And this seat is also a test of whether they can find another candidate like Joe Biden, who doesn't scare away these voters.
sentences.zh: 这个席位也是对他们能否找到像乔·拜登那样不会吓跑这些选民的候选人的考验。

sentences.en: And to win in Pennsylvania, that kind of candidate is going to have to do all the things that a regular Democrat does.
sentences.zh: 要在宾夕法尼亚州获胜，这样的候选人必须做到普通民主党人所做的一切。

sentences.en: They're going to have to win pretty comfortably in the cities.
sentences.zh: 他们必须在城市里赢得相当舒适的优势。

sentences.en: They're going to have to carry the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 他们必须拿下郊区。

sentences.en: And they're also going to have to appeal to these voters who were once Democrats but haven't been recently.
sentences.zh: 他们还必须吸引那些曾经是民主党人但最近不是的选民。

sentences.en: And those groups, they don't have a lot in common.
sentences.zh: 而这些群体之间并没有太多共同点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Democrats are basically looking for a unicorn.
sentences.zh: 民主党人基本上是在寻找一只独角兽。

sentences.en: And then along came a candidate in the primary who said, guess what?
sentences.zh: 然后初选中出现了一位候选人，他说，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I can do all of that for you.
sentences.zh: 我可以为你做到这一切。

sentences.en: It's fair!
sentences.zh: 这很公平！

sentences.en: You can get the progressivism and you can get it with the kind of packaging that's going to appeal to everyone else.
sentences.zh: 你可以得到进步主义，而且是以一种能吸引其他所有人的包装方式呈现出来。

sentences.en: And his name is John Fetterman.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫约翰·费特曼。

sentences.en: Hi, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I'm Lieutenant Governor John Fetterman, and I'm running for the United States Senate here in our beautiful Commonwealth.
sentences.zh: 我是副州长约翰·费特曼，我正在我们美丽的联邦州竞选美国参议员。

sentences.en: And the Democratic primary voters of Pennsylvania nominate him by a landslide.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州的民主党初选选民以压倒性优势提名了他。

sentences.en: Fetterman capturing 59 percent of the vote and possibly going on to win every county in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 费特曼获得了59%的选票，并可能在宾夕法尼亚州的每个县都获胜。

sentences.en: And he looks like the kind of candidate who comes from central casting, at least when it comes to trying to appeal to this voting bloc.
sentences.zh: 他看起来就像那种从选角中心走出来的候选人，至少在试图吸引这个选民群体方面是这样。

sentences.en: Standing six feet, eight inches tall in gym shorts and a hoodie?
sentences.zh: 身高6英尺8英寸，穿着运动短裤和连帽衫？

sentences.en: You'd never assume John Fetterman is a politician.
sentences.zh: 你永远不会认为约翰·费特曼是个政客。

sentences.en: He has a shaved head, goatee, his arms have tattoos on them.
sentences.zh: 他剃着光头，留着山羊胡，手臂上有纹身。

sentences.en: He almost never wears a suit.
sentences.zh: 他几乎从不穿西装。

sentences.en: He's wearing the cargo shorts.
sentences.zh: 他穿着工装短裤。

sentences.en: He's wearing the sweatshirt.
sentences.zh: 他穿着运动衫。

sentences.en: He's a big, white, burly dude.
sentences.zh: 他是个高大、白人、魁梧的家伙。

sentences.en: Look, he doesn't look like the kind of Democrat that people have grown to distruSt.
sentences.zh: 看，他看起来不像那种人们已经开始不信任的民主党人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's unpolished in his presentation, the way he talks.
sentences.zh: 他的表达方式，他说话的方式，都很不修边幅。

sentences.en: You know, getting on Twitter every morning is like starting the day with a dog turd and motor oil smoothie.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每天早上刷推特就像以一杯狗屎和机油的奶昔开始新的一天。

sentences.en: It's just, it's horrible.
sentences.zh: 真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And he's explicit about trying to appeal to white working class voters in places like northeastern Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 而且他明确表示要争取宾夕法尼亚州东北部等地的白人蓝领选民。

sentences.en: This campaign has always been about every county, every vote.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选一直都是关于每一个县，每一张选票。

sentences.en: Now, what's interesting about Fetterman is that his politics are actually pretty left, even further left than Joe Biden in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 费特曼有趣的地方在于，他的政治立场其实相当左，在很多方面甚至比乔·拜登还要左。

sentences.en: This idea that some random senator from a state with 600,000 people can hold up the Democratic will and the sense of urgency.
sentences.zh: 这种认为来自一个只有60万人口州的随机参议员可以阻碍民主党的意志和紧迫感的想法。

sentences.en: For example, he's been an outspoken advocate to get rid of the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 例如，他一直是废除阻挠议事规则的直言不讳的倡导者。

sentences.en: I don't think that's very Democratic at its core.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这在核心上是非常民主的。

sentences.en: To enact a whole range of progressive policies.
sentences.zh: 为了制定一系列进步政策。

sentences.en: Legal marijuana is serious policy for these serious times.
sentences.zh: 合法大麻是这个严肃时代的一项严肃政策。

sentences.en: He's been a big proponent of decriminalization of marijuana.
sentences.zh: 他一直是支持大麻去罪化的大力倡导者。

sentences.en: We have freed individuals who their crime was being an 18-year-old sitting in a getaway car, having no idea what was going on inside.
sentences.zh: 我们释放了一些人，他们的罪行只是作为一个18岁的年轻人坐在逃跑的车里，根本不知道里面发生了什么。

sentences.en: He is a big proponent of criminal justice reform.
sentences.zh: 他是刑事司法改革的大力支持者。

sentences.en: And the central question of this election is if the Fetterman package can get him in the door.
sentences.zh: 而这次选举的核心问题是，费特曼的这套包装能否让他敲开选民的大门。

sentences.en: Or is it enough for him to then make his case on policy, why his progressivism is actually good for these white working class voters?
sentences.zh: 或者说，他是否足以以此为基础阐述他的政策，说明为什么他的进步主义实际上对这些白人蓝领选民有好处？

sentences.en: Why his advocacy of a higher minimum wage could help them?
sentences.zh: 为什么他倡导提高最低工资能帮助他们？

sentences.en: Why it's his advocacy for a more expansive health care system that could advantage them?
sentences.zh: 为什么他倡导更广泛的医疗保健系统能让他们受益？

sentences.en: Because he thinks that those are winning points for Democrats among these voters and that too many Democrats don't even get in the door in the first place.
sentences.zh: 因为他认为这些是民主党在这些选民中获胜的要点，而太多的民主党人甚至连门都进不去。

sentences.en: So how does this actually go for John Fetterman once it looks like he's going to be the Democratic nominee for U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦约翰·费特曼看起来将成为民主党提名的美国参议员候选人，

sentences.en: Senate from Pennsylvania?
sentences.zh: 情况会如何发展呢？

sentences.en: Well, something else very important happens right before he becomes the candidate, which is that he suffers a stroke and, in his own telling, almost dies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在他成为候选人之前发生了一件非常重要的事情，那就是他中风了，用他自己的话说是差点死掉。

sentences.en: And so that means for the first few months as the Democratic nominee, he's not actually on the campaign trail, which, of course, isn't great if you're running for Senate.
sentences.zh: 这意味着作为民主党候选人的最初几个月，他实际上并没有参加竞选活动，当然，如果你在竞选参议员，这可不太好。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But he does eventually get back out there.
sentences.zh: 但他最终还是回到了竞选活动中。

sentences.en: And by late summer, Daily Producer Nina Feldman and I went and started visiting the area to see how he was playing with the voters we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 到了夏末，《每日新闻》制片人妮娜·费尔德曼和我开始走访该地区，看看他在我们谈论的那些选民中表现如何。

sentences.en: How you doing?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 好极了。

sentences.en: And so Nina went to a rally in Scranton, which is President Biden's hometown and a place that really has come to symbolize the heart of the white working class.
sentences.zh: 妮娜去参加了斯克兰顿的一场集会，那是拜登总统的家乡，也是一个真正象征着白人蓝领核心的地方。

sentences.en: My name is Nina.
sentences.zh: 我叫妮娜。

sentences.en: I'm with The New York Times with The Daily PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我来自《纽约时报》的《每日新闻》播客。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And what she found is that John Fetterman is drawing big crowds.
sentences.zh: 她发现约翰·费特曼吸引了大量人群。

sentences.en: Just chatting with folks about what brought them out today.
sentences.zh: 只是和人们聊聊是什么让他们今天来到这里。

sentences.en: What brought us out?
sentences.zh: 是什么让我们来到这里？

sentences.en: To see the big guy.
sentences.zh: 来看看那个大块头。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，电梯停了，约翰看着泰德说，嘿，你好。

sentences.zh: 但费特曼确实有真正的支持者，死忠支持者。

sentences.en: And for some of them, even his stroke is a positive.
sentences.zh: 对他们中的一些人来说，甚至他的中风也是一件积极的事情。

sentences.en: They could relate to it.

sentences.en: I have a pacemaker and a defibrillator and I can still do, you know.
sentences.zh: 我装了起搏器和除颤器，但我依然能做很多事，你知道的。

sentences.zh: 很多人一生中都经历过健康方面的挣扎。

sentences.en: I mean, I was proud of him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我为他感到骄傲。

sentences.en: He did what he could to keep going.
sentences.zh: 他尽其所能地坚持了下去。

sentences.en: And had to get back up and keep going.
sentences.zh: 而且不得不重新振作，继续前行。

sentences.en: He's just a man, you know, like he's a man's man.
sentences.zh: 他就是个普通人，你知道，他是个纯爷们儿。

sentences.en: And so Fetterman has used that image as this big, strong, Pennsylvania tough guy to develop a real contrast with his Republican opponent, Dr. Mehmet Oz.
sentences.zh: 因此，费特曼利用这种“宾夕法尼亚硬汉”的形象，与他的共和党对手穆罕默德·奥兹医生形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania needs a conservative who will put America firSt.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州需要一位将美国放在首位的保守派。

sentences.en: One who can reignite our divine spark, bravely fight for freedom, and tell it like it is.
sentences.zh: 一位能重燃我们神圣火花、勇敢为自由而战、并直言不讳的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Better known by those of us who watch television as Dr. Oz.
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些看电视的人来说，他更广为人知的身份是奥兹医生。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Oz and I approve this message.
sentences.zh: 我是奥兹医生，我认可这条信息。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And Dr. Oz is almost a perfect foil for John Fetterman.
sentences.zh: 而奥兹医生几乎是约翰·费特曼完美的衬托。

sentences.en: First of all, he's exceedingly rich.
sentences.zh: 首先，他非常有钱。

sentences.en: He most recently didn't live in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他最近才搬到宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: He's famous.
sentences.zh: 他很有名。

sentences.en: He's polished.
sentences.zh: 他很圆滑。

sentences.en: He's sharp.
sentences.zh: 他很精明。

sentences.en: And he just escaped a bruising, expensive Republican primary where his opponents had questioned
sentences.zh: 而且他刚刚从一场激烈且昂贵的共和党初选中脱身，他的对手曾质疑过

sentences.en: his MAGA credentials with the very base of white working class voters that John Fetterman says he can win.
sentences.zh: 他作为MAGA（让美国再次伟大）候选人的资历，而这正是约翰·费特曼声称他能争取的白人蓝领选民群体。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, so far, so good for John Fetterman in having Oz as his opponent.
sentences.zh: 所以，对约翰·费特曼来说，有奥兹作为对手，目前为止一切顺利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And look, he entered the general election recovering from his stroke mostly at home, but his campaign was throwing punch after punch online.
sentences.zh: 你看，他进入大选时大部分时间还在家中从脑卒中恢复，但他的竞选团队在网上发起了猛烈攻势。

sentences.en: Let me just give you one example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: Hey, Maymat.
sentences.zh: 嘿，梅梅特。

sentences.en: This is Nicole Snooki.
sentences.zh: 我是妮可·史努基。

sentences.en: His campaign hired Snooki, the former reality TV star from Jersey Shore, to make a video claiming Oz as New Jersey's own.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选团队雇佣了曾出演《泽西海岸》的真人秀明星史努基，制作了一段视频，声称奥兹是新泽西州的人。

sentences.en: I know you're away from home and you're in a new place, but Jersey will not forget you.
sentences.zh: 我知道你离家在外，身处异地，但泽西州不会忘记你。

sentences.en: I just want to let you know.
sentences.zh: 我只是想让你知道。

sentences.en: I will not forget you.
sentences.zh: 我不会忘记你。

sentences.en: And don't worry because you'll be back home in Jersey soon.
sentences.zh: 别担心，因为你很快就会回到泽西的家了。

sentences.en: This is only temporary.
sentences.zh: 这只是暂时的。

sentences.en: He flew banners over the beach in New Jersey asking Oz to come home.
sentences.zh: 他在新泽西的海滩上空拉起横幅，要求奥兹回家。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And probably most famously, I thought I'd do some grocery shopping.
sentences.zh: 最出名的可能还是这段，我想去买点杂货。

sentences.en: I'm at Wagner's.
sentences.zh: 我在瓦格纳超市。

sentences.en: Fetterman mocked a video that Oz had made during the primary in a supermarket.
sentences.zh: 费特曼嘲讽了奥兹在初选期间于一家超市拍摄的视频。

sentences.en: Asparagus, that's four dollars.
sentences.zh: 芦笋，四美元。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 胡萝卜，再加四美元。

sentences.en: That's ten dollars.
sentences.zh: 一共十美元。

sentences.en: Where he was talking about the high prices of inflation in vegetables.
sentences.zh: 当时他在谈论蔬菜价格高涨的通货膨胀问题。

sentences.en: And he started talking about shopping to buy crudités.
sentences.zh: 他开始谈论买蔬菜拼盘（crudités）。

sentences.en: My wife wants some vegetables for crudités, right?
sentences.zh: 我妻子想买点蔬菜做拼盘，对吧？

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: A very fancy sounding word for a plate of vegetables.
sentences.zh: 这听起来是个很高级的词，其实就是一盘蔬菜。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In PA, we call this a veggie tray.
sentences.zh: 在宾州，我们管这叫蔬菜拼盘（veggie tray）。

sentences.en: And if this looks anything other than a veggie tray to you, then I am not your candidate.
sentences.zh: 如果这在你眼里不是蔬菜拼盘，那我就不是你要选的候选人。

sentences.en: So all of this is playing perfectly into Fetterman's plan to embody the white working class.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都完美契合了费特曼塑造白人蓝领代言人的计划。

sentences.en: And Oz is giving him a huge assist by seeming so out of touch with that very same group of voters.
sentences.zh: 而奥兹因为看起来与那群选民完全脱节，给了他巨大的助攻。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And by the end of summer, John Fetterman is reliably ahead in polls.
sentences.zh: 到了夏末，约翰·费特曼在民调中稳步领先。

sentences.en: And in fact, at that point, he's the only Democrat in the country who appears poised to flip a Republican seat.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在那时，他是全国唯一看起来有望翻转共和党席位的民主党人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then the Republican counteroffensive begins.
sentences.zh: 然后共和党的反攻开始了。

sentences.en: He shot a teenager in cold blood, killing him for money to buy heroin.
sentences.zh: 他冷血地枪杀了一名少年，为了钱去买海洛因。

sentences.en: And John Fetterman wanted him to walk free.
sentences.zh: 而约翰·费特曼却想让他逍遥法外。

sentences.en: And it's really a two-pronged attack.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一次双管齐下的攻击。

sentences.en: John Fetterman wants to let as many criminals out of prison as he can.
sentences.zh: 约翰·费特曼想尽可能多地释放监狱里的罪犯。

sentences.en: He'd end life sentences for felony murder.
sentences.zh: 他要废除重罪谋杀的终身监禁。

sentences.en: The first prong was the issue that was the subject of so many ads, which was crime.
sentences.zh: 第一波攻势是广告中出现最多的议题，即犯罪问题。

sentences.en: When illegals commit crimes here.
sentences.zh: 当非法移民在这里犯罪时。

sentences.en: Sanctionary cities is not a policy that I very much see with it.
sentences.zh: 庇护城市政策并不是我非常认可的政策。

sentences.en: A policy that would let them back on our streets instead of deporting them.
sentences.zh: 这种政策会让他们回到我们的街道上，而不是将他们驱逐出境。

sentences.en: John Fetterman is too far left.
sentences.zh: 约翰·费特曼太左了。

sentences.en: He's dangerously liberal on crime.
sentences.zh: 他在犯罪问题上危险地激进。

sentences.en: It's true that John Fetterman is not a tough-on-crime Democrat.
sentences.zh: 约翰·费特曼确实不是那种对犯罪强硬的民主党人。

sentences.en: And there have been many that have cast themselves as that, but that's not how he's campaigned in his career.
sentences.zh: 虽然有很多人标榜自己是那样，但这并不是他职业生涯中的竞选方式。

sentences.en: And crime is a really effective strategy for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 而且犯罪议题对共和党人来说是一个非常有效的策略。

sentences.en: And it's one they use over and over.
sentences.zh: 这是他们反复使用的一招。

sentences.en: Because it really hits three critical demographic groups all at once.
sentences.zh: 因为它能同时精准打击三个关键的人口群体。

sentences.en: It appeals to voters in cities who are the ones actually suffering through increased crime.
sentences.zh: 它吸引了城市里的选民，因为他们正是犯罪率上升的实际受害者。

sentences.en: It appeals to voters in suburbs who are afraid that the increased crime in the city is creeping closer and closer to them.
sentences.zh: 它吸引了郊区的选民，因为他们担心城市里日益严重的犯罪正逐渐蔓延到他们身边。

sentences.en: And it appeals to people in more rural areas who sort of look down at those Democratic cities and can't believe how they're running things and messing things all up.
sentences.zh: 它也吸引了农村地区的民众，他们看不起那些民主党执政的城市，无法理解他们是如何治理并把事情搞得一团糟的。

sentences.en: And when I've talked to Republicans in Pennsylvania and in other states this year, they say it also is polling well with key swing voters.
sentences.zh: 今年我和宾夕法尼亚州及其他州的共和党人交谈时，他们说这个议题在关键摇摆选民中民调表现也很好。

sentences.en: This guy is not fit to serve the great people in this commonwealth of Pennsylvania for a variety of reasons.
sentences.zh: 这家伙出于各种原因，根本不适合为宾夕法尼亚州联邦的伟大人民服务。

sentences.en: First of all, John Fetterman has never had a real job in his life.
sentences.zh: 首先，约翰·费特曼这辈子从来没干过正经工作。

sentences.en: He's a giant fraud.
sentences.zh: 他是个彻头彻尾的骗子。

sentences.en: The second prong of the Republican counteroffensive was to undercut his image as a candidate of the working class.
sentences.zh: 共和党反攻的第二波攻势是削弱他作为蓝领阶层候选人的形象。

sentences.en: He dresses up like he's an industrious blue-collar worker.
sentences.zh: 他打扮得像个勤劳的蓝领工人。

sentences.en: But for him, it is a costume.
sentences.zh: 但对他来说，这只是在演戏。

sentences.en: He's playing.
sentences.zh: 他在装模作样。

sentences.en: It's make-believe.
sentences.zh: 这是在玩过家家。

sentences.en: Every day is Halloween for John Fetterman.
sentences.zh: 对约翰·费特曼来说，每天都是万圣节。

sentences.en: So they marry this attack on crime with these ideas that he's not really who he says he is.
sentences.zh: 所以他们将对犯罪的攻击与他并非他所宣称的那种人的观点结合起来。

sentences.en: John Fetterman pretends he's Pennsylvania tough, but he sponged off his rich parents till he was 49, admitting they were his principal source of income.
sentences.zh: 约翰·费特曼假装自己是宾州硬汉，但他一直靠富有的父母养活到49岁，并承认他们是他主要的收入来源。

sentences.en: Is that accurate?
sentences.zh: 这准确吗？

sentences.en: It is true, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是真的，没错。

sentences.en: So John Fetterman went to Harvard.
sentences.zh: 约翰·费特曼确实上过哈佛。

sentences.en: And after graduating from graduate school, he ended up moving back to a small town in western Pennsylvania called Braddock.
sentences.zh: 研究生毕业后，他搬回了宾夕法尼亚州西部一个叫布拉德克的小镇。

sentences.en: And he became mayor.
sentences.zh: 他当上了镇长。

sentences.en: He ran.
sentences.zh: 他参加了竞选。

sentences.en: And the mayor of Braddock earns basically no salary.
sentences.zh: 而布拉德克镇长的薪水几乎为零。

sentences.en: And he was supported financially by his parents during that period.
sentences.zh: 在那期间，他在经济上一直由父母支持。

sentences.en: They even supported a non-profit that he used to help service the city.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至资助了一个他用来服务该镇的非营利组织。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 呵。

sentences.en: And so the goal for the Oz campaign, between crime, between his Harvard education, between the fact that they said he was earning an allowance until he was in his 40s,
sentences.zh: 所以奥兹竞选团队的目标，通过犯罪议题、哈佛学历、以及他们所说的他40多岁还在领零花钱的事实，

sentences.en: was to flatten John Fetterman.
sentences.zh: 就是要彻底击垮约翰·费特曼。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And the problem for John Fetterman is that if Republicans flatten him, then is he just a liberal who happens to wear a hoodie?
sentences.zh: 约翰·费特曼的问题在于，如果共和党人击垮了他，那他是否就只是一个碰巧穿着连帽衫的自由派？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because Republicans are trying to take the very thing that Democrats have been finding so appealing about Fetterman, this ability to win over the white working class,
sentences.zh: 因为共和党人正试图夺走民主党人觉得费特曼最有吸引力的特质，即赢得白人蓝领阶层的能力，

sentences.en: and just strip him of it and say none of it was ever real.
sentences.zh: 并剥去他的伪装，声称这一切从来都不是真的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And on the calendar, in a normal campaign, a debate would be circled as a moment where you could push back,
sentences.zh: 在正常的竞选日程中，辩论会被圈出来，作为一个你可以反击的时刻，

sentences.en: where you could make the case that I'm really the candidate I've been all along, and those negative, nasty ads you've been seeing, those aren't true.
sentences.zh: 你可以借此证明我一直以来就是我所宣称的那种候选人，而那些你看到的负面、恶毒的广告都不是真的。

sentences.en: But for John Fetterman, the debate date was circled for a very different reason.
sentences.zh: 但对约翰·费特曼来说，辩论日期被圈出来的原因却截然不同。

sentences.en: He hasn't fully recovered from his stroke.
sentences.zh: 他还没有从脑卒中中完全恢复。

sentences.en: Gentlemen, thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 各位先生，感谢你们的到来。

sentences.en: And this is a debate that was held under circumstances unlike almost any other debate.
sentences.zh: 这是一场在几乎不同于任何其他辩论的环境下举行的辩论。

sentences.en: Above the moderators are two 70-inch television screens scrolling through closed captioning so he can read the questions and the answers as they're delivered,
sentences.zh: 在主持人上方有两台70英寸的电视屏幕，滚动显示实时字幕，这样他就能在问题和回答提出时阅读内容，

sentences.en: because he has auditory issues and struggles to understand what people are saying if he can't read it at the same time.
sentences.zh: 因为他有听觉障碍，如果不能同时阅读字幕，就很难理解别人在说什么。

sentences.en: Lisa, with that, let's get started, Mr. Fetterman.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，那么，让我们开始吧，费特曼先生。

sentences.en: We're going to begin with you.
sentences.zh: 我们从你开始。

sentences.en: And at this big debate, Oz and Fetterman go at each other.
sentences.zh: 在这场大型辩论中，奥兹和费特曼针锋相对。

sentences.en: I'm running to serve Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我参选是为了服务宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: He's running to use Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他参选是为了利用宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: Here's a man that spent more than $20 million of his own money to try to buy that seat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个花了超过2000万美元个人资金试图买下这个席位的人。

sentences.en: He raised taxes as mayor.
sentences.zh: 他当镇长时加税。

sentences.en: He tried to raise taxes as lieutenant governor, 46%.
sentences.zh: 他当副州长时试图加税，加了46%。

sentences.en: That's a big tax rate.
sentences.zh: 那可是个很大的税率。

sentences.en: And he's done that without paying his own taxes 67 times.
sentences.zh: 而且他这样做的时候，自己却有67次没有缴纳税款。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: The Oz rule, of course, he's lying.
sentences.zh: 奥兹规则，当然，他在撒谎。

sentences.en: It was helping two students 17 years ago to help them buy their own homes.
